''' Kevin Tyree Dyson''' (born June 23, 1975) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[wide receiver]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Utah Utes football|Utah Utes]].<ref name="pfr">{{cite web|title=Kevin Dyson|publisher=Pro Football Reference|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DysoKe00.htm|access-date=May 19, 2010}}</ref> He was selected by the [[Tennessee Oilers]] 16th overall in the [[1998 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1998 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1998/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Dyson is best known for his part in two historic NFL plays – the [[Music City Miracle]] and [[The Tackle]].<ref name="stuck">{{cite news|last=Magee|first=Jerry|title=Stuck in Music City: Dyson still fields questions on '99 postseason|work=San Diego Union-Tribune|date=January 31, 2004|url=http://www.signonsandiego.com/sports/nfl/20040131-9999_1s31panthers.html|access-date=May 19, 2010}}</ref> He and his brother [[Andre Dyson|Andre]] were the first brothers in NFL history to score [[touchdown]]s in the same game.<ref name="Redskins bio"/>

After his football career ended, Dyson earned two master's degrees and a doctorate, and became the principal of a middle school, then a high school.<ref name="nypost.com">{{Cite web|url=https://nypost.com/2019/05/26/sad-super-bowl-icon-becomes-middle-school-principal/|title = Sad Super Bowl icon becomes middle school principal|date = May 26, 2019}}</ref>

'''Kevin Darwin Greene''' (July 31, 1962{{snd}}December 21, 2020) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] and [[defensive end]] for the [[Los Angeles Rams]], [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], [[Carolina Panthers]], and [[San Francisco 49ers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1985 through 1999. He had 160 [[quarterback sack|sacks]] in his career, which ranks third among [[List of National Football League career sacks leaders|NFL career sack leaders]], and was voted to the [[National Football League 1990s All-Decade Team|NFL 1990s All-Decade Team]]. He was elected to the [[Pro Football Hall of Fame]] in 2016.

Greene played [[college football]] for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]]. He was a three-time [[All-Pro]] during his NFL playing career and was twice the [[List of National Football League annual sacks leaders|league leader in sacks]]. He was later an [[outside linebacker]]s [[Coach (sport)|coach]] for the [[Green Bay Packers]] from 2009 through 2013 and the [[New York Jets]] from 2017 through 2018.
